The microstructure of Ni alloy produced by hot isostatic pressing (HIP) and selective laser melting (SLM) using pre-alloyed Ni 41Al41Cr12Co6 spherical powders was studied by scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and high-resolution electron microscopy (HRTEM).

The alloy subjected to HIP treatment (Fig. 4a, d) has a homogeneous, fine-grained structure consisting of three phases, which are the taupe and gray grains of the β-NiAl matrix with the α-Cr phase precipitates and disperse inclusions (the white phase) of hafnium solid solution (ssHf) uniformly distributed within it.

The microstructural studies of the transverse cross-sections (Fig. 4d, e) and the top surface of the SLM layers (Fig. 5a) revealed that the SLM samples have a characteristic dendritic structure similar to that of the initial material.
Fig. 4 (c, f) shows that thermal treatment (T = 860 °C, 3 h) of the SLM samples causes coarsening and homogenization of the grain structure due to recrystallization.

Pre-alloyed spherical powders based on β-NiAl, which had been produced by centrifugal plasma sputtering of the electrode, were used as initial material.

The cylindrical samples (D = 10, H = 60 mm) were fabricated by HIP on a HIRP 10/26–200 gasostat (Abra AG, Switzerland) under isothermal exposure at 1300 °C and 150 MPa. The capsule was manufactured from low-carbon steel 20; argon was used as a pressure transmitter.

other.scanning_strategy: bidirectional laser scanning, scanning vector rotated by 90° for each new layer

evidence.quote: Samples 10 × 10 × 10 mm in size were fabricated using an SLM 280 setup (SLM Solution, Germany) equipped with a 400 W YLT fiber laser. Bidirectional laser scanning was used to construct the samples; the scanning vector was rotated by 90° for each new layer. The laser scanning rate was 200 mm/s; laser intensity, 325 W; spot size, 80 µm; hatch distance, 0.2 mm; and layer thickness, 160 µm.
The SLM samples were subjected to thermal treatment in a VSl-16–22-U vacuum furnace (VakETO, Russia) at 860 °C, a residual pressure of 10⁻⁵ MPa, and isothermal exposure time of 3 h.

X-ray powder diffraction analysis of spherical powders revealed no α-Cr phase and showed 100% content of nickel monoaluminide with the lattice parameter of 0.2887 nm, which agrees well with the diffraction data.
The size of Cr-rich fine precipitates ranges from 20 to 45 nm. The EPMA analysis of nanosized precipitates showed the following composition (% at.): Cr, 82.28; Al, 8.98; Ni, 5.5; and Co, 3.24.

The increased chromium content in the alloy being higher than the solubility limit (~7 at%) in β-NiAl, as well as non-equilibrium crystallization, results in formation of thin interlayers (400…500 nm thick) of the degenerate Cr(Co)e eutectic in the interdendritic space.
Besides, nano-sized particles (size 100–150 nm) of the hafnium-based phase being precipitating in these interlayers.

The alloy subjected to HIP treatment (Fig. 4a, d) has a homogeneous, fine-grained structure consisting of three phases, which are the taupe and gray grains of the β-NiAl matrix with the α-Cr phase precipitates and disperse inclusions (the white phase) of hafnium solid solution (ssHf) uniformly distributed within it. The grain size of the β-NiAl matrix ranges from 15 to 40 µm.

attributes.location: along β-NiAl grain boundaries (large), in β-NiAl matrix grain bulk (small)
attributes.composition: Ni 6.2 at.%, Al 7.6 at.%, Cr 82.7 at.%, Co 3.5 at.%

evidence.quote: Large α-Cr inclusions, which have an elongated shape and range in size from 2 to 5 µm, are predominantly distributed along the boundaries of β-NiAl matrix grains and have been formed from the Cr(Co)e phase as a result of its segregation by the action of high temperature and pressure during HIP. Smaller α-Cr precipitates less than 2 µm in size are distributed in the bulk of the β-NiAl matrix grain.

attributes.composition: Ni 7.5 at.%, Al 1.7 at.%, Cr 4.9 at.%, Co 1.4 at.%, Hf 84.6 at.%

evidence.quote: Nanosized ssHf particles 100–500 nm in size are irregularly precipitated within large the α-Cr phase inclusions.

EPMA of the phase components (Table 2) confirmed that the composition of the central portion of the dendrites corresponds to the solid solution of the β-NiAl phase. Chromium content in β-NiAl exceeds the solubility limit and is equal to 8.7 at%, while cobalt content remains constant (~7 at%) regardless of the consolidation method used.
Thickness of the degenerate Cr(Co)e eutectic interlayers between the first-order branches ranges from 400 to 500 nm, being less than 150 nm between the second- and third-order.

attributes.composition: Ni 8.5 at.%, Al 1.5 at.%, Cr 5.4 at.%, Co 2.1 at.%, Hf 82.5 at.%

evidence.quote: Dispersed particles of the ssHf phase, which are systematically precipitated in thin interlayers of a degenerate eutectic, are less than 100 nm in size.

EPMA analysis (Table 2) of the central portion of dendrites showed that thermal treatment makes chromium excess (~1 at%) release from the β-NiAl phase into the interdendritic space. As a result, chromium content decreases (from 8.7 to 7.5 at%) down to the solubility limit in β-NiAl.

evidence.quote: The microstructural studies of the surface and the cross-section of spherical powder (Fig. 2a, b) demonstrate that all particles have a typical dendritic microstructure. The dendrites consist of the first- and second-order branches with the cross-section size of 1…5 µm.

Homogeneous precipitation and growth of the spherical Guinier-Preston zones rich in Cr (size < 5 nm) on concentration fluctuations of dopants in the β-NiAl matrix by spinodal decomposition was detected in the range of 20–450 °C.
Prismatic dislocation loops 10–25 nm in size with a stacking fault are formed from a vacancy cluster in the β-NiAl grain at 750 °C.
